evals.query: When a photo fails to upload, our photo backup app shows: 'Error 0x80042: The operation could not be completed due to an unexpected server-side condition. Please try again later or contact support if the problem persists.' Rewrite it, and write versions for these cases too: no internet connection, the account's storage is full, and the file is over 2 GB.
expected_behavior: Each message says what happened and what the person can do next, in plain words, with no error code in the main text.
Each message is specific to its cause (server problem, no internet, storage full, file over 2 GB) rather than one generic message reworded.
Button labels are specific verbs that match the next step (for example 'Try again', 'Get more storage') rather than 'OK'.
Titles and bodies are short: a title of a few words and a body of one or two short sentences.
Uses one consistent term for the thing being uploaded (photo, file or item) across all messages.
Presents the messages in a form that is easy to compare, such as a table with title, body and buttons per case.

evals.query: Write all the copy for our meditation app's onboarding: three intro screens, the screen before we ask for notification permission, and the free trial screen of the paywall (7-day free trial, then 59.99 a year).
expected_behavior: Each intro screen carries one idea, with a short title and at most one or two short sentences.
The notification screen names a concrete benefit and says it can be changed later, before the system prompt appears.
The trial screen states plainly the price, the trial length, when billing starts and how to cancel.
Primary buttons say what happens next where it matters (permission and trial), and every screen that asks for something offers a clear way to decline or skip.
Avoids hype and filler (for example 'amazing', 'unlock your potential') and keeps one voice across the screens.
Lays the copy out screen by screen with title, body and buttons clearly separated.
